import Mathlib

-- Precondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def insertionSort_precond (v : List Int) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start precond
  True
  -- !benchmark @end precond

-- !benchmark @start auxcode
/-- Insert `x` into the (already sorted) list `l`, keeping it sorted. -/
def ins (x : Int) : List Int → List Int
  | [] => [x]
  | y :: ys => if x ≤ y then x :: y :: ys else y :: ins x ys

/-- Insertion sort: sort the tail, then insert the head. -/
def isort : List Int → List Int
  | [] => []
  | x :: xs => ins x (isort xs)
-- !benchmark @end auxcode

-- Main function definitions
def insertionSort (v : List Int) (h_precond : insertionSort_precond v) : List Int :=
  -- !benchmark @start code
  isort v
  -- !benchmark @end code

-- Postcondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def insertionSort_postcond (v : List Int) (result : List Int) (h_precond : insertionSort_precond v) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start postcond
   List.Sorted (· ≤ ·) result ∧ result.Perm v
  -- !benchmark @end postcond

-- !benchmark @start lemma
theorem ins_perm (x : Int) (l : List Int) : (ins x l).Perm (x :: l) := by
  induction l with
  | nil => simp [ins]
  | cons y ys ih =>
    by_cases h : x ≤ y
    · simp [ins, h]
    · have h1 : (ins x (y :: ys)).Perm (y :: x :: ys) := by
        simpa [ins, h] using ih.cons y
      exact h1.trans (List.Perm.swap x y ys)

theorem mem_ins {a x : Int} {l : List Int} (ha : a ∈ ins x l) : a = x ∨ a ∈ l := by
  have := (ins_perm x l).mem_iff (a := a)
  have : a ∈ x :: l := this.mp ha
  simpa using this

theorem sorted_ins (x : Int) (l : List Int) (hs : List.Sorted (· ≤ ·) l) :
    List.Sorted (· ≤ ·) (ins x l) := by
  induction l with
  | nil => simp [ins]
  | cons y ys ih =>
    rw [List.sorted_cons] at hs
    by_cases h : x ≤ y
    · rw [show ins x (y :: ys) = x :: y :: ys by simp [ins, h]]
      rw [List.sorted_cons]
      refine ⟨?_, List.sorted_cons.mpr hs⟩
      intro b hb
      rcases List.mem_cons.mp hb with rfl | hb
      · exact h
      · exact le_trans h (hs.1 b hb)
    · rw [show ins x (y :: ys) = y :: ins x ys by simp [ins, h]]
      rw [List.sorted_cons]
      refine ⟨?_, ih hs.2⟩
      intro b hb
      rcases mem_ins hb with rfl | hb
      · exact le_of_lt (lt_of_not_ge h)
      · exact hs.1 b hb

theorem sorted_isort (l : List Int) : List.Sorted (· ≤ ·) (isort l) := by
  induction l with
  | nil => simp [isort]
  | cons x xs ih => exact sorted_ins x (isort xs) ih

theorem perm_isort (l : List Int) : (isort l).Perm l := by
  induction l with
  | nil => simp [isort]
  | cons x xs ih =>
    exact (ins_perm x (isort xs)).trans (ih.cons x)
-- !benchmark @end lemma

-- Proof content
theorem insertionSort_postcond_satisfied (v : List Int) (h_precond : insertionSort_precond v) :
    insertionSort_postcond v (insertionSort v h_precond) h_precond := by
  -- !benchmark @start proof
  exact ⟨sorted_isort v, perm_isort v⟩
  -- !benchmark @end proof

- **auxcode**: `ins x l` inserts `x` before the first element `≥` it; `isort` sorts the tail recursively then inserts the head — a standard recursive insertion sort.

- **lemma**:

  - `sorted_ins`: inserting into a sorted list keeps it sorted. The `x ≤ y` branch uses transitivity against the head bound; the other branch uses `mem_ins` plus `lt_of_not_ge` to bound `y ≤ x`.
  - `sorted_isort` / `perm_isort`: inductions over the list using the two lemmas above.
- **proof**: `⟨sorted_isort v, perm_isort v⟩`.
